scientific_queries.note: Audit of C45: does its comparison test annotation value, or merely granularity?

subagent_note: None dispatched: the round attacks the programme's load-bearing claim and ends with that claim downgraded to indeterminate rather than either confirmed or refuted.
the_concern: C45 compared a two-way additive model built on drug IDENTITY against a ridge built on PATHWAY annotation, i.e. fine granularity against coarse granularity, which is nearly guaranteed to favour the fine one and does not show whether the annotation carries information

decisions.H253_annotation_does_add: not established - my pre-registered criterion rested on the uncontrolled contrast and is withdrawn

what_this_overturns.the_framing_not_the_numbers: with a common encoding the additive comparator scores 6.00%, below identity at 7.87%, so C45's -10.12 pp did not reproduce; and identity versus pathway is a tie (+0.38 pp), so 'fine beats coarse' also fails to appear
what_this_overturns.status_of_the_headline: 'the annotation model is useless' has never had a matched-information comparator; now that it has one, the answer is indeterminate rather than refuted

honest_reading: random features absorb about a third of the apparent annotation gain and the remainder is not distinguishable from a capacity effect at this sample size, so neither 'annotation adds real signal' nor 'the gain is merely capacity' is established
limits: 40 splits with 130+41 dimensions is underpowered, so the null on pathway versus random may simply reflect sample size
the random block was drawn once, not averaged over repetitions
pathway annotation has only 41 dimensions, so its information ceiling is low by construction
retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI
next_gates: average over many random blocks and increase the number of splits to narrow the pathway-versus-random interval

register_updates.C71: new and central: C45 is a granularity comparison and annotation value is indeterminate
register_updates.SYNTHESIS: the headline gains a prominent caveat

mutations_outside_episode: research/SYNTHESIS.md (caveat added to the headline and to the refuted table)
